findings.reason: the Deliverable is the node's endpoint and the gate contradicts it, so an implementation that reads the Deliverable alone passes cases one to three and fails case four, and the exception the code's own record mark exists to protect would be removed.
findings.text: the Deliverable says "the run's live pointer is retired and its worktree released" without exception, while the fourth done-when case requires that a pointer written by a newer attempt on the same run keeps that pointer and its worktree; the two statements disagree on what the endpoint is, and the literal Deliverable would strand a newer attempt mid-run

findings.reason: a worker reading the section as the semantic authority may re-implement or rewrite a working guard; recording that the endpoint already holds, and that the deliverable is the regression test, is what directs the node to verify and test rather than repair.
findings.text: the Deliverable presents the retirement as behaviour to build, but it already holds at HEAD: `reckon/crew/pending_landing.py` releases the marked pointer and calls `merge.release_landed_worktrees` when a finished landing is on the remote, and `reckon/crew/promotion.py` writes the mark that scopes the release to the attempt it names; the plan's own open followup f-wftl-008 records "§29 is delivered as a regression test, because the defect no longer reproduces at main", but the section states no such thing while naming the module as a write path

response_events.note: §29's Deliverable now scopes retirement to the pointer the finished attempt wrote, and keeps a pointer written by a newer attempt and its worktree, matching the fourth case.
§29's Why now states the retirement already holds at main and that the section delivers the regression test that pins it, including the newer-attempt case.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/pending_landing.py` exists in the repository, and the sections §29's Why cites (work-flows-to-the-lane §24, a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker §29, a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan §41) all resolve in docs/plans/.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §29's fourth case requires a live pointer written by a newer attempt to survive the finished landing, while the Deliverable says "the run's live pointer is retired" with no such exception.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §29's evidence is the section's evidence fragment, the same durable convention the plan's other landed sections use, not a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test file and the module write path name the behaviour, carrying no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the Deliverable's stated endpoint is contradicted by its own fourth case, and the section presents as work to build a retirement that `reckon/crew/pending_landing.py` already performs at HEAD.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §29 names one deliverable: a finished pending landing retires the run's pointer and releases its worktree, with an unfinished one keeping both.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §29 is named by the plan's only open followup (f-wftl-008, whose title is "Build §9, §22 and §29" and whose recommended invocation builds §29), and it declares no dependency on a section whose output it consumes.
